title: Grading three lenses
intro: The summary named six benchmarks and four measurements and gave the ordering they produce. This level gives the items themselves, the scoring rules, the numbers on each distribution, and the places where the figures separate the lenses less cleanly than the text does.

chapters.title: A word the model must compute but never says
chapters.body:
Every item in the six sets is built around one constraint. The concept looked for must be something the model has to compute: absent from the prompt's surface, and different from the answer the model will give [[intermediate-concept-benchmarks]]. It must also have a single-token name, since the lens holds a vector only for tokens in the vocabulary [[single-token-limitation]]. One position per item is fixed in advance as the place to read.

The multihop set is fifty two-hop factual questions [[multihop-benchmark]]. "the color of the planet fourth from the Sun is" requires computing Mars before answering "red". Items are chosen so that the trigger word and the answer rarely co-occur without the bridging entity, which makes retrieval unlikely. The read position sits immediately before the answer.

The multilingual set is fifty-four prompts written entirely in another language, such as ‘Lo opuesto de "grande" es ’ [[multilingual-benchmark]]. Four intermediates are looked for per item: the language, the relation, and the English forms of the input and output words — Spanish, opposite, big, small. The prompt never names its language, so the token Spanish in a readout indicates detection rather than copying [[shared-multilingual-representation]].

The order-of-operations set is fifty-five arithmetic expressions such as (2 + 3) × 4 [[order-of-operations-benchmark]]. Two intermediates are scored per item, the partial result and the pending operation, with single-token synonyms accepted: 5 or five, × or times.

The poetry set is fifty-two original couplets, read at the newline between the lines [[poetry-benchmark]]. After "The soldier held his final, rattling breath,\n" the check is for "death": the rhyme is fixed and the second line is still unwritten [[rhyme-planning]].

The typo set is ninety-six sentences ending on a common misspelling, such as "...learn a second langauge." The correct spelling is looked for at the final fragment of the misspelled token [[typo-benchmark]]. At that position the model is predicting whatever follows the typo, so recovery of "language" indicates internal recognition rather than imminent output.

The association set is fifty short passages that depict a concept through behavior without naming it [[association-benchmark]]. The passage about the coffee mug kept for eleven months is scored for grief at the closing period. No single token is the trigger; the concept has to be assembled from accumulated context.

chapters.title: Scoring a ranked list
chapters.body:
An intermediate counts as recovered at $k$ when it appears among the top $k$ tokens of the lens readout at any layer, and pass@$k$ is the fraction of intermediates recovered [[pass-at-k-auc]]. The clause "at any layer" does real work. The score takes the best depth in the network, so a lens is not penalized for surfacing a concept in only a narrow band.

Pass@$k$ is measured at seven values of $k$: 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100. Those points are plotted against $\log k$, and the area under the curve is normalized so that a method always ranking the intermediate first would score 1 [[fig-52]].

The Jacobian lens leads on all six distributions, and the ordering below it is the logit lens, then the tuned lens, everywhere [[jacobian-lens]].

The size of the lead varies by a factor of several. Against the logit lens it is 0.81 to 0.77 on multihop and 0.68 to 0.65 on association, a few points in each case [[logit-lens]]. It is 0.71 to 0.53 on multilingual, 0.80 to 0.58 on poetry, and 0.83 to 0.52 on typo.

The tuned lens scores 0.18 on poetry and 0.11 on association [[tuned-lens]]. Those are the two distributions whose read position is followed by an uninformative token, a newline and a period, and the tuned lens is fitted to match the model's next-token distribution. The paper offers that as the explanation rather than as a measured cause.

On multihop, order of operations and typo the tuned lens closes much of its gap at large $k$, crossing the logit lens somewhere past $k = 20$. Its weakness on those three is a failure of ranking, not the intermediate being absent from the readout altogether [[j-lens-vector]].

One caveat belongs to the plot rather than the result. In three panels the legend box covers part of the tuned-lens curve, so its mid-range values there are read off the visible endpoints. The qualitative version of the same comparison, six prompts with all three lenses printed layer by layer, sits beside these curves [[fig-51]].

chapters.title: Asking whether the direction matters
chapters.body:
Ranking a token highly is not evidence that the model computes with that direction, so two interventions follow.

The first takes each lens's vector for the intermediate token, projects the residual stream's component along it to zero, and records the KL divergence this induces on the model's output [[ablation-kl-effect]], [[j-lens-ablation]]. A larger divergence means the direction mattered more to the answer [[kl-divergence]].

The bars run about 2.12 for the J-lens on multihop against about 0.93 for the logit lens and 0.88 for the tuned lens — the doubling the text reports. Multilingual gives 0.91, 0.67 and 0.48. Poetry gives 0.59, 0.23 and 0.34, and there the tuned lens edges above the logit lens [[fig-53]].

Three qualifications sit with that figure. It covers three of the six distributions. On poetry the J-lens error bar overlaps the tuned lens's, so the ordering inside that group is not separated. And the caption and the body text disagree about where the projection is applied: the caption says all positions, with the poetry items excluded at the target position, while the body describes the readout position alone.

The second intervention exchanges one intermediate for another in lens coordinates at $\alpha = 1$, then asks whether the model's top-1 output flips to the answer the swapped-in concept implies [[swap-success-rate]], [[lens-coordinate-swap]], [[swap-strength-alpha]]. A probability shift that does not reach the top of the distribution counts as a failure.

Run at three model scales, the J-lens flips 0.54 of items on Haiku, 0.70 on Sonnet and 0.70 on Opus [[fig-54]], [[claude-model-family]]. The logit lens gives 0.34, 0.48 and 0.40; the tuned lens 0.16, 0.42 and 0.26. The weakest J-lens number still exceeds the strongest number anywhere else in the chart.

Two things the chart does not show are worth stating. Success does not rise monotonically with scale, since Opus matches Sonnet on the J-lens and falls below it on the other two. And at Sonnet the logit and tuned intervals overlap, so the figure separates the J-lens from that pair without separating the pair.

chapters.title: The measure the J-lens comes last on
chapters.body:
The comparison the tuned lens was built to win is reported next: agreement between each lens's readout distribution and the model's own distribution over the next token [[fig-55]], [[j-lens-readout]].

Three quantities are named at each layer. KL divergence between the two distributions, the entropy of each lens's readout, and top-1 accuracy, the fraction of positions where the lens's highest-scoring token is also the model's [[next-token-prediction]].

The tuned lens is the best match at every depth. The paper attributes this to construction rather than to insight, since matching the output distribution is the objective its per-layer affine maps were fitted to. The J-lens is the worst, carrying higher KL than even the uncorrected logit lens through most of the network.

The section states that ordering in terms of KL. It names entropy and top-1 accuracy as measures without saying how the three lenses rank on them, so the reported result rests on one of the three quantities.

The paper's reading is that anticipating the output and exposing the computation behind it are different targets, and that this figure measures the first. That is a defense of the design rather than a finding: it holds only if the earlier recovery and intervention results stand. What the J-lens is built to surface is content the model is disposed to put into words if asked, which need not be what it is about to say [[verbalizable-representation]].

Depth here is reported on the paper's usual convention, twenty-five evenly spaced layers renumbered 0 to 100 so that layer numbers read as percentages [[layer-percentage-indexing]].

chapters.title: Where the three lenses agree
chapters.body:
The last comparison drops the external target. Each pair of lenses is compared to the other directly, layer by layer, on three quantities [[inter-lens-agreement]].

The first is the mean cosine between the two methods' vectors for the same vocabulary token, averaged over the vocabulary. The second is the symmetric KL between their readout distributions. The third is their top-1 agreement rate. The last two are averaged over held-out pretraining-style text [[fig-56]].

Four layer ranges fall out, and they line up with the workspace boundaries located elsewhere in the paper by unrelated statistics [[layer-bands]].

Below layer 33, no pair agrees on readouts: top-1 agreement is near zero and symmetric KL is high for every pairing [[sensory-layers]]. The logit and tuned vectors nonetheless sit at a cosine near 0.9. The tuned lens is affine, a linear transform plus a learned bias, and the cosine sees only the linear part. Stripping the bias out collapses the KL between the two readouts to near zero at these depths, which means the tuned lens's linear map is effectively the identity there and its whole advantage comes from the bias — a term that does not read the input at all [[tuned-lens-bias-term]]. J-lens vectors are close to orthogonal to both, which the paper attributes to their being confined to a low-rank subspace at these depths [[early-layer-lens-degeneracy]].

From roughly layer 38 to 58, the J-logit cosine climbs from near zero to about 0.7 over some twenty layers, while their KL stays near its peak and top-1 agreement stays low [[workspace-layers]]. The directions align before the readouts do. This is the band where the J-lens most often surfaces concepts the logit lens misses.

From roughly 62 to 92, the J-logit KL falls monotonically and their top-1 agreement is the first pairing to rise appreciably above zero. The tuned lens stays the outlier on both readout measures.

In the final few layers all three collapse together: cosine approaches one, KL drops to zero, top-1 rises to one [[motor-layers]]. The averaged Jacobian is approaching the identity there, so every lens is reduced to the same next-token readout [[jacobian-approaches-identity]].
